paper text.text:
Put $H_2=B+bc+de$ and suppose it is nonplanar.
By Lemma~\ref{r1:triangle-minor},
$B+ab+ac+ad+ae+bc+de$ is a minor of $G$.
Thus $H_2$ has no $K_5$ minor. Let $B'$ be an
allowed minor of $B$ with $B'+bc+de$ nonplanar.
The graph $B'+ab+ac+ad+ae+bc+de$ is still a minor
of $G$, so Lemma~\ref{r1:matching-test} makes
$B'+ab+ac+ad+ae$ nonplanar. Thus $\Psi_3\cup B'$
fails both tests of Lemma~\ref{r1:missing-a-criterion}.
Taking $B'=B$, minimality gives $G=\Psi_3\cup B$, and
Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms}, with attachments
$b,c,d,e$ and added edges $bc,de$,
includes $B$ among $26{,}633$ forms.
Every resulting graph other than $\mathfrak T_{54}$
is toroidal or has a $K_5$ minor or a proper
nontoroidal minor~\supp{E21}, so
$G\cong\mathfrak T_{54}$.
\end{proof}

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ...

disjoint twin triples.meaning: Section 6 assumes any two twin triples share exactly one vertex
